stopped_items: STOP fired at read 1 (a): GovTrack /api/v2/vote answers HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare managed challenge (server cloudflare, cf-mitigated challenge, HTML 'Just a moment...') to curl AND to Node fetch, both carrying the D5 headers. Per the STOP table nothing was built. Items 1-4 did not run, FIX-1372 stays open, and there was no ff and no deploy.
Reads 1 (b), (c) and (d) did not run. Same host, same challenge. 2 of the 6 budgeted GovTrack GETs were used, both on (a).

Read 1 (e) was DENIED by the auto-mode permission classifier. Exact command: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command, running Invoke-WebRequest -Method Head -UseBasicParsing -Uri 'https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1192/vote_119_2_00256.xml' inside a try/catch that prints the status and headers. It was not retried through curl or anything else, so senate.gov's status today is NOT recorded.

Read 1 (f) was substituted. I sent GET /v3/senate-vote?limit=1 in place of /v3/house-vote?limit=1, because the house-vote URL cannot answer the stated question (is there a Senate family). One congress.gov request, as budgeted.
Reads 0, 2, 3, 4 and 5 did not run. They feed the build the STOP cancelled. No prod reads, and no db-query of any kind.

Item 0 filed nothing. FIX-1372's 'Done looks like' (a Senate source the nightly can read) already owns this finding, because GovTrack being challenged is a fact about one candidate source, not a new defect.
